public_rationale: He said that in 2025 all we would have are agent demos. In 2025, agent products were in real, paid production use. Anthropic says Claude Code became generally available in May 2025, was used by firms such as Netflix and Spotify, and reached a $1 billion revenue run rate by November. Salesforce reported more than 9,500 paid Agentforce deals and a 70% quarterly rise in accounts in production. That is more than demos. In fairness, general-purpose agents were still unreliable: the best agent automated only 2.5% of real freelance projects. If 'demos' meant only 'do anything' agents, the claim is closer to true. But the sentence as written is not limited that way.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'demos' as covering all AI agent products, not only general-purpose ones.
Coding agents and customer-service agents might count as the 'narrow use cases' he allowed in the previous sentence.
Run-rate revenue is a company-reported figure, not audited annual revenue.
